Analysis by Richard Cowan

In today’s Vancouver Sun, my friend Ian Mulgrew reported that Marc Emery has agreed

in a “plea bargain” to a five-year term to be served in a Canadian prison.

See

The Paupers of Pot and the Politics of Cannabis Prohibition In Canada. The Other

Cases Raise Questions That Canada Must Answer. Will Canada Murder Michelle

Rainey?

and links

Mulgrew has written extensively on the subject and knows all of the parties personally.

See

Behind the BS: Ian Mulgrew’s Bud Inc. – A Look Inside BC’s Big Biz.

As a Canadian, he is outraged.

He says, “Our extradition law puts Canadian citizens at the mercy of foreign governments and

judges can't do much about it. Emery is being forced to accept a deal because not only are two

of his friends in jeopardy if he doesn't, but also to go south for an unfair trial would mean

serving as much as 20 years in prison, perhaps more.

One of his friends, for example, was handed a 30-year sentence for growing 200 plants. This is

wrong.

If Emery has been breaking the law and must be jailed, our justice department should charge

him and prosecute him in Canada. It's time for Justice Minister Rob Nicholson to step in and

say, sorry, Uncle Sam, not today - not ever.”

Although this sentence is an outrage against any sense of justice, it is also as good a deal as

can be expected under the circumstances. Had Marc chosen to fight it out to the bitter end,

he would almost certainly have lost and ended up dying of old age – or a violent death – in

the American Gulag.

As a part of the deal, charges against Marc’s co-defendants, Greg Williams and my very

dear friend Michelle Rainey are expected to be dropped. Greg did nothing more than sell

seeds to an American nark, while sitting at a desk in Vancouver. Michelle, who would die of

Crohn’s Disease if she were sentenced to even a year in the US, did nothing more

“criminal” than many others among Marc’s numerous employees.

Of course, Emery was paying his Canadian taxes and was even recommended by Health

Canada as a source of seeds for Canadian medical marijuana exemptees.

Although the US is clearly the aggressor in this case, the Canadian government has failed

to defend its sovereignty and the basic rights of its citizens. If the US says it wants aCanadian, Canada’s rather slow court system may dither a while, but the current

Canadian government has just two real constituencies, the Canadian narks and the US

government.

See

Three Separate Canadian Stories May 13, 2003. You Connect The Dots. Steve Tuck’s

Hearings; Canadian Justice Minister Grovels Toward Gomorrah, DC That Is. And A

Subtle Twist In The Party Line.

and

Wake Up Canada! 2006 Canadian Professional Police Association Political Agenda.

“Prime Minister of Canada to Open the CPPA Annual Legislative Conference”

I became completely disgusted with Canadian “justice” during the refugee hearings for

Steve Kubby and Steve Tuck. When they took Tuck – catheter attached – from a Vancouver

ER in handcuffs, I finally realized the level of barbarism to which a civilized people can

descend.

See

Steve Tuck Taken from Vancouver ER In Handcuffs to US Border. Will the Feds Kill

Him?

It is worth noting that this deal has not been completely finalized, and there is an

extradition hearing scheduled for January 21. But it is believed that the US prosecutors

have agreed to let Marc serve his time in Canada, and I have always thought that Greg and

Michelle were essentially hostages. It is not uncommon for the narks to charge family

members in order to extort a plea bargain, but the federal system is so rigged against the

defendants that they have little chance of winning. Marc would have almost certainly lost if

he tried to fight it.

Mulgrew says that the US is insisting that Marc serve the full five years, in accordance with

US practice. Canadian sentences for most crimes are much shorter than in the US, but it is

the US that is out of line with the rest of the world. That is one reason that we have 5% of

the world’s population, but 25% of the prisoners.

See

The Drug Testing and Rehab Rackets Keep Prisons Full. From California to the UK The

Results Are Tragic – And Expensive. Did Michael Vick Find A Loophole?

Mulgrew concludes, “It's a scandal.

Emery is being made a scapegoat for an anti-cannabis criminal law that is a monumental

failure. In spite of all our pricey efforts during the last 40 years, and all the demonization of

marijuana, there is more pot on our streets, more people smoking dope and more damage

being done to our communities as a result of the prohibition.

There is a better way and every study from the 1970s Le Dain Commission onward has urged

change and legalization.

Regardless of what you think of Emery, he should not be facing an unconscionably long jail

term for a victimless, non-violent crime that generates a shrug in his own country. Emery isfacing more jail time than corporate criminals who defrauded widows and orphans and longer

incarceration than violent offenders who have left their victims dead or in wheelchairs.”
